#### H-S1-03 — The across-patient Stage 1 basis lets discovery / LOPO / patient-specific coefficients live in one coordinate system — but LOPO is label transfer on a transductive atlas, not inductive deployment.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Discovery, LOPO and patient-specific coefficients share one transductive Stage 1 coordinate system.
- Gate not: LOPO is label transfer on a transductive atlas, not inductive deployment or a raw-expression deployment benchmark; donor-downsampling refits are not inductive.
- Alternatives: ALT-TRANS (partial)
- Blocking tasks: W2.1 (done); W2.6 (open)
- Figures: design, §8
- Analyses: D3, D4, D17

Current evidence:

- **supports** D3 compares, within one Stage 1 coordinate system, each patient's apparent within-patient AUPRC with the same patient's LOPO AUPRC on the same representation; the high-opportunity gap threshold is the median gap, 0.381. ([2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites#2](devlog/2026/2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites.md), 2026-07-24)
- **supports** 2026-08-26 addendum: the D9 LOPO train-fold StandardScaler cancels the all-cell gene z-score, so D9 LOPO is effectively inductive for continuous gene scaling only, while the DR representations remain transductive. ([2026-08-25_repository-audit#1](devlog/2026/2026-08-25_repository-audit.md), 2026-08-25)
- **qualifies** Transductive optimism is small but consistent in sign: per-patient inductive-minus-refit median deltas lie between −1.29 and −0.05 pp across the 18 tuned/L2 summaries (all negative). Examples: PCA40 tuned L2 −0.30 pp (7/7 patients lower), PCA20 tuned L1 −0.54 pp (7/7), FA20 tuned L1 −1.29 pp (6/7), FA40 tuned L1 −0.10 pp (4/7; range −3.83 to +3.31). The largest single-patient drops: FA40 P03 tuned L1 −3.83 pp and FA40 P09 L2 −3.38 pp. The P09-out FA basis matches FA7 at |r| 0.75 (many-to-one R² 0.98). ([2026-10-08_d17-basis-variant-pilot#2](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d17-basis-variant-pilot.md), 2026-10-08)

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))

But only 729 of the 20,274 robust pairs keep at least half their size inside supported patient x cell type strata (median retention ratio 0.15), and 1,665 of 1,801 cards have a larger within-patient cell-type eta2 than patient eta2. In normal cells, factor x surface-protein associations are mostly predicted cell-type (identity) axes; the 25 strongest are myeloid, erythroid and progenitor markers (CD11a, CD18, CD33, CD200, CLEC12A, CD123, CD71, CD151), led by HVGs (500) FA40 factor 3 x CD11a (median within +0.809, 7/7, pooled +0.829, patient x cell type +0.254). Of the 8,474 robust pairs, 7,053 exceed their card's isotype reference and 1,797 keep at least half their size inside patient x cell type strata (median retention 0.26). Pooled malignant associations are therefore largely between-patient (patients nested in batch; P03 holds 758 of the 1,569 malignant cells). ### Q2

#### H-S0-01 — Malignant-vs-non-malignant structure is recoverable inside curated prior gene spaces (single genesets and biology groups), not only in broad HVG bags.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Descriptive for old34: malignant-vs-normal structure is recoverable inside curated program gene spaces and transfers above constant-score no-skill AP for typical supported patients on the transductive basis.
- Gate not: Not that curated priors beat any N genes (Null Model 1, size-matched HVG and exact single-score comparators are missing); control bags are technical floors, not the biological null.
- Alternatives: ALT-GENESET (open); ALT-SEL (open); ALT-NPAT (open); ALT-TRANS (open)
- Blocking tasks: W4.2 (open); W4.1 (open); W3.3 (open)
- Figures: V2A, V2F1, D1, D2, D1DD1, D1DD9
- Analyses: D1, D3, D12

Current evidence:

- **supports** D3 provisional taxonomy over 41 biological panels (current 2026-09-11 tables): shared_plus_patient_specific 17, truly_shared 13, null_or_unresolved 7, patient_only 2, cohort_illusion 1, hidden_transfer 1. ([2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites#1](devlog/2026/2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites.md), 2026-07-24)
- **supports** 783 atlas cells (640 biological DR + 41 biological direct-gene + 96 control DR + 6 control direct-gene; 5,481 patient evaluations): median lift > 0 in 670/783 and P20 lift > 0 in 639/783; all 47 panels have at least one P20-positive representation; control DR median lift > 0 in 89/96 cells. ([2026-09-11_d1-atlas-783-d1e-d1f#1](devlog/2026/2026-09-11_d1-atlas-783-d1e-d1f.md), 2026-09-11)

#### H-S0-02 — The old34 GSEA dictionary is not an alias of HVG 3,000.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: The old34 dictionary and the HVG anchors are not interchangeable Stage 0 panels; the control rows are technical floors shown beside the programs.
- Gate not: Not that the programs beat size-matched HVG or random gene sets run through the same Stage 2 grid.
- Alternatives: ALT-GENESET (open)
- Blocking tasks: none
- Figures: D12
- Analyses: D12

Current evidence:

- **supports** D12: full_34 (2,719 genes) vs HVG3,000: overlap 948 genes, Jaccard 0.199, 1,771 old34-only genes (65.1% of old34), fold-enrichment 1.81x, hypergeometric p = 1.31e-101. Against HVG 500 / 1,000 / 10,000 the Jaccard is 0.057 / 0.098 / 0.219. ([2026-09-03_d12-d13-gsea-hvg-lowsupport#1](devlog/2026/2026-09-03_d12-d13-gsea-hvg-lowsupport.md), 2026-09-03)

- H-S1-01 (supported_descriptive): Stage 1 method and K are not interchangeable inside a panel; transfer can flip with geometry × regularization. Full record under Q3.

- H-S1-04 (supported_descriptive): Patients can be aggregated on a shared Stage 1 basis when per-patient factor-score distributions overlap. Disjoint supports would be separate subtypes. Full record under Q1.

#### H-S2-06 — On a frozen Stage 1 basis, held-out AUPRC rises with the number of Stage 2 training cells. That is a depth curve for this cohort, not a forecast for sequencing a new patient.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Descriptive: on a frozen transductive basis, held-out AUPRC can rise with Stage 2 training-cell depth at a fixed patient mix where the probe is not collapsed at fixed C.
- Gate not: Not a Stage 1 learning curve and not evidence that sequencing another patient would move AUPRC; cell depth only; not a patient-count curve; flat L1 curves at fixed C are all-zero collapse, not absence of signal.
- Alternatives: ALT-PEN (partial); ALT-TRANS (open); ALT-NPAT (partial)
- Blocking tasks: W6.1 (done); W6.2 (open)
- Figures: D15A–B
- Analyses: D15, D15b

Current evidence:

- **supports** Full-training refits match the D1 atlas within 0.000164 AUPRC. Apoptosis promax K40 (L2) median lift: 7.65 pp at 500 cells (about 13 training malignant cells), 9.28 at 1,000, 11.52 on the full set. ([2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve#1](devlog/2026/2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve.md), 2026-10-02)
- **supports** Allograft promax K40 (EN) median lift is 0 through 2,000 cells, then 1.67 / 3.14 / 8.81 / 12.56 pp at 5k / 10k / 25k / full. ([2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve#2](devlog/2026/2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve.md), 2026-10-02)
- **qualifies** IFN-alpha PCA40 and FA40 (L1, C=1e-4) stay at prevalence (median lift 0) at every subsample up to 25,000 cells; on the full set PCA reaches 11.08 pp and FA 0. With C fixed, the L1 entry threshold is about 1.6 SD at 25k cells, so these curves are flat by construction. ([2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve#3](devlog/2026/2026-10-02_d15-cell-count-learning-curve.md), 2026-10-02)
- **qualifies** With C retuned per training set, lift is positive with one supported training patient for all four representations (median 4.45-8.79 pp), and the primary paired gain k = 2 → 6 is small next to its uncertainty. Median gain [95% CI], patients with gain > 0, mean gain [95% CI]: ([2026-10-08_d15b-full-design#1](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d15b-full-design.md), 2026-10-08)

  | representation | median gain [95% CI] | patients > 0 | mean gain [95% CI] |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | PCA40 | 1.67 [-0.44, 2.89] | 5/7 | 1.16 [-0.15, 2.43] |
  | FA40 | 0.30 [-0.53, 4.18] | 4/7 | 1.75 [-0.48, 4.42] |
  | apoptosis | 1.14 [-0.53, 2.38] | 5/7 | 2.49 [-0.01, 6.42] |
  | allograft | 2.34 [0.14, 2.73] | 6/7 | 1.27 [-0.15, 2.46] |

  Only allograft's median-gain CI excludes 0. The curves are not monotone: PCA40 peaks at 9.30 at k = 4 and ends at 8.71; FA40 is 6.66 at k = 4 and 6.20 at k = 5.
- **qualifies** Per-patient gains k = 2 → 6 range from −2.80 (P02, FA40: 17.85 → 15.05) to +13.32 pp (P03, apoptosis: 28.54 → 41.86). The largest gain in each representation is in a highest-prevalence patient (PCA40 P04 +2.94, FA40 P04 +8.30, apoptosis P03 +13.32, allograft P02 +3.09); P02 loses lift on both IFN-alpha representations (−1.81, −2.80). P01 and P06 stay within −0.53 to +1.14 pp. At k = 6, per-patient lift ranges from 0.06 (P06, PCA40) to 41.86 pp (P03, apoptosis). ([2026-10-08_d15b-full-design#2](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d15b-full-design.md), 2026-10-08)
- **qualifies** Power law (primary validation, tuned median): reportable for 1 of 4 representations. Apoptosis passes (fit k ≤ 4 predicts 9.51 at k = 5 vs observed 10.31 [1.96, 35.80]; a = 9.80 pp, b = 4.45 pp, c = 1.68); its asymptote lies below the observed k = 5 and 6 medians, so it describes a plateau. PCA40, FA40 and allograft fail with c at its bound (allograft also b at bound and no rise). With CIs this wide the check is weak. ([2026-10-08_d15b-full-design#3](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d15b-full-design.md), 2026-10-08)

#### H-I-01 — Constant-score average precision equals malignant prevalence exactly under the implemented metric.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Metric contract: constant-score no-skill AP = π under the implemented metric (proved and checked in D6).
- Gate not: A metric contract, not a biology claim; AP and a single clinical cutoff are separate statements.
- Alternatives: none
- Blocking tasks: none
- Figures: D6A, guide §1
- Analyses: D6

Current evidence:

- **supports** D6: constant all-healthy and all-malignant scores both reproduce malignant prevalence exactly as AP; they differ only in threshold utility (P06: accuracy 0.9865 vs 0.0135, AP = π = 0.0135 for both). ([2026-08-31_d6-d9-meeting-followup#1](devlog/2026/2026-08-31_d6-d9-meeting-followup.md), 2026-08-31)
- **supports** All 757 all-zero supported (cell, fold) pairs at the selected regularization have |lift| <= 5.6e-17, i.e. constant-score AP equals the held-out prevalence. ([2026-10-08_w7-atlas-strip-factor-explorer#1](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_w7-atlas-strip-factor-explorer.md), 2026-10-08)

- H-S0-03 (open): Bottom-up manuscript-axis panels (Set B atomic / family union / leave-one-family-out) identify which dictionaries add malignancy signal. Full record under Q3.

- H-S0-04 (open): Pooled old34∪expanded bags (no per-geneset identity) still carry shared malignancy, and size-matched HVG 11,421 is the fair bag-level control. Full record under Q3.

- H-S2-01 (open): PI Q1 — a robust shared model exists: high discovery AP, high aggregate LOPO, consistent per-patient lift, stable selected factors. Full record under Q1.

#### H-S2-09 — In MRD single-cell data both the malignant training-cell count and the healthy-to-malignant ratio limit held-out transfer; downsampling healthy (donor) training cells, stratified by predicted cell type and trajectory position, with C retuned per condition, raises held-out lift through Stage 1 geometry or negative-class composition rather than through the n-dependent penalty.

- Verdict: **open** since 2026-10-09 ([2026-10-09_w8-healthy-downsampling-plan](devlog/2026/2026-10-09_w8-healthy-downsampling-plan.md))
- Gate supports: Would need, on the cohort fixed by W8.5 and under the pre-registered plan (workstreams/W8_new_cohort/healthy_downsampling_plan.md): a nested downsampling recipe that beats the full-data probe on median and P20 lift under tuned L1 and L2 in the inductive scope, with pooled AP quoted beside them; a ratio effect at a fixed malignant count in the count-by-ratio grid; a mechanism read-out (Stage 1 geometry or healthy-cell composition) that tracks the gain; and the same direction on the new patients.
- Gate not: Not supported by any fixed-C result (D10 is an all-zero L1 collapse, so AP returns to π by construction); not a gain that the full-data probe reaches somewhere on an extended C path (ALT-NREG), that appears only in the transductive scope or only in the highest-prevalence patients, or that rests on an in-sample choice of scheme and retention level; not a donor-shortcut statement (H-S2-04); not inductive deployment, causal biology or recurrence risk.
- Alternatives: ALT-NREG (open); ALT-PEN (open); ALT-PREV (open); ALT-CT (open); ALT-TRANS (open); ALT-SEL (open)
- Blocking tasks: W8.5 (done); W8.6 (in_progress); W8.7 (blocked)
- Figures: none
- Analyses: none

Current evidence:

- (none)

- H-S1-05 (not_supported): High-prevalence patients P02/P03/P04 shape the Stage 1 loadings, not only Stage 2 labels and selection. Full record under Q1.

#### H-S2-04 — Donor-healthy abundance can induce a shortcut; downsampling donor-healthy training cells tests that.

- Verdict: **not_supported** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Not supported as stated: at the selected fixed C, donor downsampling collapses L1 probes to all-zero, so AP returns to prevalence by construction; that is a regularization artifact, not a donor test.
- Gate not: Not that the model is invariant to donor-versus-recipient origin, and not that it learns donor identity; no performance-level donor test exists until condition-specific C (W4.6).
- Alternatives: ALT-DONOR (open); ALT-PEN (open)
- Blocking tasks: W4.6 (open)
- Figures: D10E, D11B, D11C
- Analyses: D10, D11

Both are about 0.98-0.99 at 50%. ([2026-08-03_narrative-guide-donor-correction#1](devlog/2026/2026-08-03_narrative-guide-donor-correction.md), 2026-08-03)

- H-S0-02 (supported_descriptive): The old34 GSEA dictionary is not an alias of HVG 3,000. Full record under Q2.

#### H-S1-01 — Stage 1 method and K are not interchangeable inside a panel; transfer can flip with geometry × regularization.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))

#### H-S1-02 — A no-DR (direct-gene) probe on the same Stage 0 panel is the right Stage 1 control. DR is not universally additive.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Descriptive: the direct-gene probe on the same panel is the right no-DR control; DR helps pooled AP far more often than patient-equal median or P20 lift, and its gains concentrate in the highest-prevalence patients.
- Gate not: Not that DR universally adds value; best-DR selection is in-sample, the comparison is asymmetric while Stage 1 is transductive, and the one-score proxy is not a fair pathway-score baseline. Quote pooled AP, median lift and P20 lift together.
- Alternatives: ALT-SEL (open); ALT-PEN (open); ALT-TRANS (open)
- Blocking tasks: W3.3 (open); W3.4 (open); W2.1 (done)

- Analyses: D9, D1e, F4, D1DD9, D23, D24

#### H-S2-08 — The IFN-alpha PCA40-vs-FA40 patient-coverage gap at the selected C is a Stage 2 L1 threshold effect on related directions in one shared subspace (PC8, FA7), not missing Stage 1 structure.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))

- Gate supports: Descriptive and transductive: at the selected C the coverage gap tracks the L1 entry threshold on related directions (PC8, FA7), and L2 or per-fold tuned C on the same FA scores recovers the patients that L1 drops.

- Figures: D8, F3, F6, F9

With C tuned, FA40 has no all-zero unit and PCA40 is all-zero in 5% of k = 2 units only. ([2026-10-08_d15b-full-design#4](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d15b-full-design.md), 2026-10-08)

#### H-I-03 — Stage 1 loadings can be used as sign-oriented descriptive gene lists, but L1-selected factor indices are not unique biological programs.

- Verdict: **supported_descriptive** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: Descriptive: sign-oriented within-factor loading ranks are readable gene lists when the sign orientation and the Stage 2 penalty (L1, L2 or elastic net) are stated.
- Gate not: Not that loadings cannot be looked at; not that a factor index is the IFN-alpha gene program; L1-selected factor indices are not unique biological programs; not SHAP or LIME.
- Alternatives: ALT-ROT (partial); ALT-SEED (open); ALT-DEGEN (partial)
- Blocking tasks: W5.1 (done); W5.4 (open)
- Figures: F2d, F3
- Analyses: D5, F9, D18

Current evidence:

- **supports** D5 grounded 45 factors (843 factor-to-gene rows, 135 patient-overlap rows) as sign-oriented top-10 positive and negative gene lists. Factor IDs are comparable only within one representation, and the interferon signaling, hypoxia, IFN-gamma signaling and p53 top factors are selected in 0 or 1 of 13 folds. ([2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites#3](devlog/2026/2026-07-24_d1-d5-diagnostic-suites.md), 2026-07-24)
- **supports** Orientation: PC8's L1 coefficient is negative in every active fold (−0.040 to −0.064), so the malignant-leaning pole is the negative group (TXNIP, IFITM2, TENT5A, NCOA7, TRIM5, ELF1). FA7 (positive coefficient; r −0.685 with PC8) carries the same contrast with flipped raw signs. IFI27 and IFITM2 are both interferon-stimulated genes on opposite poles. ([2026-10-02_f9-ifna-pc8-loadings#2](devlog/2026/2026-10-02_f9-ifna-pc8-loadings.md), 2026-10-02)
- **supports** After orientation by sign(beta), FA7 (sign +1, active only in P03 and P04) lists the same poles as PC8: malignant TENT5A +0.171, BST2 +0.156, IFITM2 +0.155, GBP2 +0.143, IFITM3 +0.135, IFI44L +0.134; normal IFI27 -0.209, PSME2 -0.172, PSMA3 -0.162, IFI30 -0.152, CD47 -0.129, TRIM26 -0.124. ([2026-10-08_d18-factor-cards#3](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d18-factor-cards.md), 2026-10-08)
- **qualifies** PC8 and FA7 are not individually identifiable: PC8's relative eigengap is 0.055; FA7's determinacy is 0.649 (below 0.707) with effective_k 36 of 40; Tucker phi between PC8 and FA7 is 0.691, below the 0.85 fair band, although FA7 has R2 0.888 on the PCA40 basis. Across the bundle, 36 of the 119 selected drivers have low determinacy and 61 a small eigengap; none is degenerate, and 13 (all factosig_promax) carry the scale_outlier caveat. ([2026-10-08_d18-factor-cards#4](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d18-factor-cards.md), 2026-10-08)
- **qualifies** Review A: factosig_promax loadings.npy is the pattern matrix (cov(gene, score) = L·Φ with relative residual 2.4e-4). For IFN-alpha promax K40, pattern and structure top-10 genes overlap with median Jaccard 0.18 (min 0.05), and 136 of 780 score pairs have |r| > 0.5 (max 0.924), so a single promax factor should not be named as a driver. ([2026-10-08_literature-reviews#2](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_literature-reviews.md), 2026-10-08)
- **qualifies** Review A: IFN-alpha FA40 has effective_k 36 (factors 37-40 are all zero), and FA7 and FA8 have factor-score determinacy 0.649 and 0.618, below 0.707. PC8 is 81% explained by FA7 + FA8 (R² 0.806) and congruent with neither (Tucker φ −0.691 and +0.577). ([2026-10-08_literature-reviews#3](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_literature-reviews.md), 2026-10-08)

#### H-S2-07 — Team hypothesis (a): PCA orthogonality pushes later components beyond P03 while FA keeps allocating factors to the highest-prevalence patient.

- Verdict: **retired** since 2026-10-08 ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Verdict history: 2026-10-08 retired ([2026-10-08_d19-regularization-contract](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d19-regularization-contract.md)); 2026-10-08 retired ([2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_research-spine-adopted.md))
- Gate supports: None: retired. The IFN-alpha PCA versus FA coverage gap is explained by Stage 2 L1 at a fixed C (H-S2-08), and Stage 1 is label-blind.
- Gate not: do not cite as a mechanism
- Alternatives: none
- Blocking tasks: none
- Figures: none
- Analyses: F3, F6, D7

Current evidence:

- **contradicts** D7: over 38 panels x 7 patients the median PCA40 − FA40 lift in P02 is −2.76 pp (FA usually better), and MHC class I in P02 gives FA40 47.44 vs PCA40 0.00 pp, so FA is not generally biased toward P03. ([2026-08-31_d6-d9-meeting-followup#5](devlog/2026/2026-08-31_d6-d9-meeting-followup.md), 2026-08-31)
- **contradicts** F6: FA7 is the strongest training-fold FA coordinate in every fold, and its held-out single-factor lift is P02 18.06 pp and P07 6.97 pp (PC8 15.94 and 11.08); within-patient r(PC8, FA7) runs from −0.575 to −0.722. FA does not allocate the axis to P03 only. ([2026-09-17_team-feedback-f1-f7#4](devlog/2026/2026-09-17_team-feedback-f1-f7.md), 2026-09-17)
- **contradicts** FA40 covers P02 and P07 as soon as the stored C is raised by 5% or tuned, through FA7, a direction related to PCA40's PC8 in the shared IFN-alpha subspace (stored K40 scores: r(PC8, FA7) −0.685 and r(PC8, FA8) +0.580; PC8 has many-to-one R² 0.920 on the FA40 scores; D18), not the same axis; the gap needs no FA allocation toward the highest-prevalence patient. ([2026-10-08_d19-regularization-contract#5](devlog/2026/2026-10-08_d19-regularization-contract.md), 2026-10-08)
